positions.title: Graduate Assistant
positions.description:
Research:

+Data reduction of large data sets
+Statistical analysis of V447 Lyr - a dwarf nova cataclysmic variable
+Probing physics of accretion disk of dwarf nova
+Defining characteristic profiles of outburst phenomena in system

Teaching:

+Development of lab curriculum for students
+Managing lab equipment and stockroom
+Aiding students by running study/homework help sessions

positions.title: Lab Assistant
positions.description:
East Tennessee State University Observatory

+Set up laboratories for students
+Secured and unsecured the grounds every night
+Installed necessary software on observatory computers
+Volunteered at several public outreach events, including local science fairs, Science Olympiad events, public viewings at observatory once a month

positions.title: Astrophysics Research Assistant
positions.description:
East Tennessee State University, Department of Physics and Astronomy

Project: Diagnostics of the Hanle effect for stellar atmospheres

+Use of spherical trigonometry to develop geometries for stars
+Developed code in C for numerical integration of line scattering over surface of star

positions.title: REU Researcher
positions.description:
Computational Laboratory at University of South Florida
Focus: Condensed matter theory and Computational physics

Project: Development of Embedded Atom Potential for Aluminum for Simulation of Materials at extreme conditions
+Developed database of experimental data for density functional theory calculations
+Pressure curve simulation and optimization
+Generated potential function to fit database of experimental and theoretical data
+Tested potential function via molecular dynamics simulations

honors.title: Finalist - Best Student Poster Award - 2017 Joint Nanoscience and Neutron Scattering User Meeting
Co-chair of Deep Data in Materials Characterization Workshop at Center for Nanophase Materials Sciences

organizations.name: Society of Physics Students, ETSU Chapter
organizations.description:
Along with the president, I built the current SPS at ETSU up from a very sparse membership to an active group with 15+ dedicated members.

Our group focuses on public outreach for physics and astronomy and volunteers at several community events as well as local schools to incite interest in the fields.
